Highlights:
In addition to being backwards compatible on the Nintendo Switch 2, an enhanced version of the game for the system was released on July 24, 2025 under the name Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV, which includes new game modes along with visual enhancements, improved framerate, and support for CameraPlay and GameShare. [33]
...
Like with its predecessor, Super Mario Party Jamboree features the traditional Mario Party gameplay as the main mode of the game; players traverse a game board to collect coins in order to purchase Stars. The gameplay is overall more similar to Mario Party Superstars than Super Mario Party, sharing many of the same rules and mechanics, such as the dice rolling between one and ten and the occurrence of Bonus Minigames, where the coins won are doubled. Various new mechanics are introduced, including Jamboree Buddies, allies that grant the player a unique ability and trigger a space's effect twice upon landing, which serve as a revamped version of the ally mechanic from Super Mario Party. When a player passes by an unaffiliated Jamboree Buddy on the board, all players participate in a Showdown minigame, where the one who passed them is granted a slight advantage and the winner recruits the Jamboree Buddy.
...
Additionally, either Party Rules or Pro Rules can be selected for a game. With Pro Rules on, some mechanics of the game will be adjusted, aiming to create a more competitive game, which includes removing Hidden Blocks and locking Boo's coin steal to 15 coins. 

Pro Rules use a locked ruleset, with the only option that the player can have before starting ... game is the ability ... turn off mini-games help (unavailable in matchmaking) and motion-controlled minigames. The ruleset includes the game lasting for 12 turns only, one Bonus Star that is announced at ... start of the game, and minigame selection ... set to vote. The only three Bonus Stars that can be revealed are the Happening Star, Slowpoke Star, and Sightseer Star.
...
Other changes include: 

- Lucky Spaces only giving a choice of either a Double Dice or 10 coins, with players choosing what they want instead of a random roulette.
- Unlucky Spaces always giving 7 coins to the last-place player.
- Chance Time Spaces not appearing, instead being changed to a different space. 

- Additionally, depending on the board, other spaces are changed as well, such as Lucky Spaces replacing Blue Spaces.
...
- Players always betting a set number of 20 coins when a player lands on a VS Space, and the player who lands on the space being able to choose the minigame instead of it ... chosen randomly.

Highlights:
Jamboree TV contains all of the new modes that have been added to this version of the game. It features four modes, two of which are altered versions of existing modes and two of which are entirely new modes that take advantage of new features of the Nintendo Switch 2.
...
Mario Party functions mostly the same, though if the CameraPlay feature is enabled, the players' faces can be seen at all times on the UI next to their characters, as well as during certain events such as Chance Time. Mouse minigames may also appear as 2-vs.-2 minigames, though they may be toggled off alongside motion-controlled minigames. While Pro Rules does not reappear in this version of Mario Party, two new rules have been added, being Tag Team Rules and Frenzy Rules.
...
Tag Team Rules function similarly to the Team Match and Tag Battle modes in previous games, in which players are split into teams of two. Each team shares their coins, Stars, and items. Whichever team has more coins and Stars by the end is the winner. Jamboree Buddies do not appear in this ruleset, being replaced by a unique item that can only be obtained with these rules, known as the Together Dice. This item calls the user's teammate to their space and both they and their teammate roll one of the Dice Blocks. The two then move together the combined number of spaces from both Dice Blocks. In this state, items, Stars, and space effects are doubled, similarly to the effect of a Jamboree Buddy. When both players from the same team land on the same space, their team obtains five coins. Some spaces are also replaced with a new type of space exclusive to this mode known as the Rally Space. Other than accommodating for these spaces, other changes are also made to the space layouts on every board, such as the removal of VS Spaces and a larger amount of spaces with negative effects, such as Red Spaces and Unlucky Spaces.

Other Homestretch events, such as duels starting if two players land on the same space, can also happen from the start. Additionally, only one Bonus Star is given out at the end of the game.

The Payday Triple Dice is an item in Super Mario Party Jamboree. It is a more powerful variant of the Payday Double Dice, being a set of three solid gold dice. This item allows the player to roll three Dice Blocks (much like a Triple Dice), with the player receiving coins equal to the total amount rolled (much like the Plus Block from the first Mario Party). The player can potentially get 3-30 free coins with the Payday Triple Dice, along with an additional 20 coin bonus for matching numbers or 50 coin bonus for matching sevens similar to the Triple Dice. 

Mario's Jamboree Buddy ability dice roll also adds to the total amount of coins for a maximum of 79 coins (with a roll of matching sevens for 21 coins, the 50 coin bonus, and an 8 from Mario). 

Payday Triple Dice can be purchased from the Gold Shop in Rainbow Galleria for 15 coins (7 during a Flash Sale, or 30 if the player has a Markup Sticker) and from Kamek's Shop in Goomba Lagoon during Pro Rules. It is also one of the dice items that can be randomly obtained from paying 10 coins at the Dice Shop pit stop on Roll 'em Raceway. Outside of that, it can rarely appear from an Item Bag or Item Space.

The Mario Party™ series is back with even more ways to get festive! The Super Mario Party™ Jamboree – Nintendo Switch™ 2 Edition + Jamboree TV game is giving partygoers new modes and minigames using the Joy-Con™ 2 mouse controls, HD rumble 2, and the system’s built-in microphone. This enhanced version of the game offers some interesting upgrades, so let’s get into them.
...
Two new rulesets have also been added to Mario Party mode: Tag-Team Rules and Frenzy Rules!

In Tag-Team Rules, it’s a 2-on-2 battle across the board! Work together with your teammate to collect coins and Stars. You might also find Together Dice, which only appear in this ruleset. Call your teammate to your location to help you roll two dice and move that many spaces—together. This means items, Stars, and even space effects are doubled!

Now, in Frenzy Rules, you only have five turns to win—so, the pressure is on. Each player will start with 50 coins, a Double Dice item, and a Star. Challenge your rivals to duels and see who will take those precious coins.
